name: Voskhod
dispatch: The Voskhod spacecraft was a Vostok pushed past its design, and it shows exactly what improvisation under deadline looks like. To make the one-seat capsule carry more, engineers pulled out the ejection seat — the crew's only escape — and for the first flight left out the pressure suits too; for the second they bolted on an inflatable airlock so a cosmonaut could go outside. It scored the first multi-person crew and the first spacewalk, the last two firsts the Soviet program would claim. But it had no margin left, and after the near-disaster of its second flight it was retired — a stopgap that did its narrow job and was wisely not asked to do more.
description: A modified Vostok refitted to carry up to three cosmonauts. Two crewed flights — Voskhod 1 (first multi-crew) and Voskhod 2 (Alexei Leonov’s first spacewalk in 1965). Pushed beyond the design margin and was retired in favour of Soyuz.
